description: A junior CS student who is comfortable with high-level data structures and collaboration but feels intimidated by low-level C memory management and debugging.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This student has some_prior_exposure, so a targeted refresher on C memory mechanics ensures they are ready for kernel-level assignments.
nodes.description: A review of C-language memory management (pointers, malloc, free) and basic data structures to ensure a solid foundation for systems-level programming.
nodes.title: C and Memory Review for Systems

nodes.description: Overview of OS services, system calls, and the fundamental distinction between user and kernel mode.
nodes.title: Operating System Structures & Services
nodes.personalizationRationale: This foundational knowledge is required for all students, including those with some_prior_exposure, to understand system protection.

nodes.description: Examination of monolithic, layered, and microkernel architectures used in modern operating systems.
nodes.title: Kernel Architecture Design
nodes.personalizationRationale: Building on the student's some_prior_exposure, this node explores the structural design choices of modern kernels.
Process management is a core requirement that bridges the student's some_prior_exposure to deeper OS abstractions.
nodes.title: Process Abstraction & Lifecycle
nodes.description: Exploration of the process abstraction, including Process Control Blocks (PCBs) and the process lifecycle (ready, running, waiting).
Practical implementation of Inter-Process Communication using shared memory and message-passing protocols.
nodes.title: Inter-Process Communication (IPC)
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required for the project sequence, this node utilizes the student's some_prior_exposure to implement communication primitives.

nodes.description: Comparison of user threads vs. kernel threads and various threading models (many-to-one, one-to-one).
nodes.title: Threading Models & Libraries
nodes.personalizationRationale: Threading models are essential for the upcoming multi-threaded projects and build on the student's some_prior_exposure background.

nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms
nodes.description: Analysis of scheduling algorithms including FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, and Priority Scheduling.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core topic requires students with some_prior_exposure to analytically model CPU scheduling performance.

nodes.title: Midterm Review (Ch. 1-5)
nodes.description: A comprehensive review session covering Chapters 1-5 in preparation for the midterm exam.
nodes.personalizationRationale: As a student with some_prior_exposure, this review helps synthesize varied concepts before the first major examination.

nodes.title: The Critical Section Problem
nodes.description: Defining race conditions and implementing software/hardware solutions like Mutexes and Semaphores.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Synchronization is a key cumulative concept that every student must master, building on some_prior_exposure to coding.

nodes.description: Deep dive into classic problems like the Bounded-Buffer, Readers-Writers, and Dining Philosophers problems.
nodes.title: Classic Synchronization Problems
nodes.personalizationRationale: Applying synchronization primitives to classic problems is essential for the final exam and benefits from some_prior_exposure.

nodes.description: Understanding the four conditions for deadlock and applying the Banker's Algorithm for deadlock avoidance.
nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization & Avoidance
nodes.personalizationRationale: Even with some_prior_exposure, understanding formal deadlock prevention is a mandatory component of OS theory.

nodes.description: Exploring paging, segmentation, and the structure of hierarchical and hashed page tables.
nodes.title: Physical Memory & Paging
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required for the memory management project, this node leverages some_prior_exposure to explain physical address translation.
Virtual memory management is a complex core topic where some_prior_exposure helps in understanding hardware-software interaction.
nodes.title: Virtual Memory & Page Replacement
nodes.description: Focus on demand paging, page faults, and replacement algorithms like FIFO, Optimal, and LRU.

nodes.title: I/O Systems & Performance
nodes.description: Survey of I/O hardware, interrupt-driven I/O, and the Kernel I/O subsystem architecture.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This capstone block ensures students with some_prior_exposure understand how the OS interacts with physical device drivers.
File systems are a mandatory topic tested on the final; some_prior_exposure assists in grasping file metadata and storage.
nodes.title: File System Implementation
nodes.description: Analysis of file system structures, directory implementation, and disk block allocation methods.
Final comprehensive review of all course material from Chapters 1-15 in preparation for the cumulative final exam.
nodes.title: Cumulative Final Review
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the cumulative nature of the final exam, this review synthesizes knowledge for students with some_prior_exposure.
